evidenceTiers.regulatory: Approved product for its labeled indication only; not proof of molecular effect separation
evidenceTiers.human-comparison: Human pharmacology or acute-effects comparison, not therapeutic efficacy
evidenceTiers.preclinical: Cell and/or animal findings; no validated human treatment

records.desiredEffect: Neuronal structural plasticity and disease-relevant behavioral outcomes
records.observed: JRT promoted cortical spine growth and behavioral effects in preclinical tests with reduced hallucinogenic potential relative to LSD.
records.boundary: No demonstrated human efficacy or assurance that hallucinations are absent in people.

source.title: Molecular design of a therapeutic LSD analogue with reduced hallucinogenic potential

records.mechanism: Multiple targets; not simply CB1 agonism
records.desiredEffect: Seizure control for specific approved epilepsy indications
records.studyDesign: Regulatory approval supported by clinical trials
records.observed: FDA-approved purified CBD treats seizures in Lennox-Gastaut syndrome, Dravet syndrome and tuberous sclerosis complex without THC-like intoxication.
records.boundary: This does not show that removing intoxication from THC preserves THC's effects, nor that CBD treats other conditions.

source.title: FDA regulation of cannabis and cannabis-derived products

records.comparator: Other mu-opioid agonists including fentanyl and morphine
records.relationship: synthetic opioid example (not isolated from opium)
records.mechanism: Mu-opioid receptor signaling, brain entry and receptor trafficking
records.undesiredEffect: Respiratory depression, tolerance, withdrawal and strong reinforcement
records.studyDesign: Preclinical receptor assays and rodent studies
records.observed: DFNZ showed analgesia with markedly different respiratory, tolerance and reinforcing profiles in the reported rodent experiments.
records.boundary: Not demonstrated safe, effective or non-addictive in humans. Some reinforcement occurred. Nitazene chemical family carries serious overdose concerns.

source.title: A µ-opioid receptor superagonist analgesic with minimal adverse effects

records.relationship: cell-specific mechanism, not a new drug
records.undesiredEffect: Head-twitch response (limited rodent proxy for hallucination)
records.observed: Layer-5 pyramidal-neuron 5-HT2A signaling was necessary and sufficient for induced synaptic remodeling but dispensable for head twitch in tested mice.
records.boundary: Head twitch cannot establish the presence or absence of human hallucinations; no human antidepressant separation is demonstrated.

source.title: 5-HT2A receptors in layer 5 pyramidal neurons mediate the neuroplastic but not the hallucinogenic effects of psilocybin

records.desiredEffect: Antidepressant-like and anxiolytic-like responses in rodents
records.studyDesign: Structural biology, in vitro pharmacology and rodent behavior
records.observed: A 5-HT1A-selective 5-MeO-DMT analogue retained selected mood-related behaviors without the tested hallucinogenic-like readout.
records.boundary: No proof of efficacy or non-hallucinogenic action in humans; 5-MeO-DMT is not interchangeable with DMT.

source.title: Structural pharmacology and therapeutic potential of 5-methoxytryptamines

records.desiredEffect: Fear extinction, synaptic plasticity and antidepressant-like animal outcomes
records.undesiredEffect: Monoamine release, hyperthermia and stimulation proxies
records.studyDesign: In vitro experiments and rodent behavior
records.observed: R-MDDMA showed plasticity and behavioral effects without several classic MDMA pharmacology/readouts at the tested doses.
records.boundary: Human PTSD efficacy and long-term safety are not established. Therapeutic psychological experience may contribute to MDMA-assisted therapy.

source.title: R-MDDMA is a Safer Analogue of MDMA with Therapeutic Potential

records.mechanism: Monoamine transporters and other serotonergic activity
records.desiredEffect: Acute comparative pharmacology (not a demonstrated treatment)
records.undesiredEffect: Longer and stronger adverse subjective effects and visual alterations
records.observed: MDA had longer and stronger subjective and more psychedelic-like effects than MDMA at equimolar doses in the studied volunteers.
records.boundary: A direct acute-effects comparison is not proof of therapeutic benefit or a safe therapeutic MDA formulation.

source.title: Acute effects of MDMA, MDA, lysine-MDMA, and lysine-MDA in a randomized crossover trial

records.mechanism: Metabolite pharmacology distinct from parent ketamine; mechanisms under study
records.desiredEffect: Candidate antidepressant outcomes from animal studies
records.observed: The tested metabolite was tolerated without appreciable dissociation or sedation at the investigated doses in healthy volunteers.
records.boundary: Phase 1 did not establish antidepressant efficacy in patients; this is not an approved treatment.

source.title: A Phase 1 Assessment of (2R,6R)-Hydroxynorketamine in Healthy Volunteers

records.desiredEffect: Mechanistic mapping of exposure and effects (no therapeutic outcome tested)
records.undesiredEffect: Variable exposure, autonomic and subjective effects
records.observed: Human CYP2D6 variation changed MDMA and MDA exposures and some response measures; MDA is a metabolite, not merely a comparison drug.
records.boundary: Observed metabolic variation is not evidence that increasing or blocking MDA improves therapeutic outcomes.

source.title: CYP2D6 function moderates the pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics of MDMA

records.relationship: approved enantiomer comparator, not a non-dissociative derivative
records.undesiredEffect: Dissociation, sedation, misuse risk and blood pressure elevation
records.observed: Esketamine is a regulated, FDA-approved treatment for specified depression indications; its known dissociation and sedation hazards remain.
records.boundary: Regulatory approval is not evidence that dissociative effects can be eliminated without changing benefit; monitoring requirements apply.
